articleTitle: Modeling of Susceptibility Equipement in System Problem
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents the development of simple models for susceptibility of all kind of equipment components, these models being matched for a system analysis.

articleTitle: Conception of a VIRC for Susceptibility Test
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents the method used to define a Vibrating Intrinsic; Reverberation Chamber (VIRC) which allows us to make susceptibility tests on PCB and equipment in the microwave frequency band (1-18 GHz). Also, we discuss about the use of VIRC results in order to assess the susceptibility to other environments (free space, real cavity).

articleTitle: Experimental Optimization of CCA Thresholds in Wireless Sensor Networks in the Presence of Interference
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Performance of Carrier Sense Multiple Access with Collision Avoidance (CSMA/CA) protocol implemented on a Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) in the presence of interference are here investigated. In particular, attention is focused on the Clear Channel Assessment (CCA) method, and on the choice of CCA threshold. The purpose of the work is to provide helpful information and hints for designers to be considered and applied in order to optimize the use of CCA algorithm and the setup of CCA threshold, in the presence of in-channel additive white gaussian noise interference. To this goal, a number of meaningful experiments is conducted, through a suitable testbed and measurements executed both at physical and medium access control layer.

articleTitle: Cellular Phone Detection by Leaky Line Antennas Aboard Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A system for detection and localization of cellular phone operations on-board aircraft is proposed. The system is based on the utilization of a coaxial cable with apertures on the shield, or a leaky line antenna (LLA), as a receiving antenna, and the localization is carried out by the “a priori” knowledge of the position on the slots along the cable shields by assuming that the active cellular phone transfers the maximum power into the nearest slot. The proposed system is validated by experiments.

articleTitle: Investigations of the Effect of Different Network Architectures and Sources of Disturbances on the Operability of PLC in One-to-One Scale Laboratory Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Due to the fact the low-voltage supply networks are not designed for communication and data transmission but for effective energy transportation some difficulties may occur when installing a PLC system. The challenge is even greater because network topology and the so called “series elements” such as switches, fuses, energy meters etc. have different effects on the transmission's efficiency. Other sources of challenges are the shunt type normal household goods like washing machines, microwave ovens, compact fluorescent lamps etc. These kinds of elements can be found on any low voltage network. All the appliances connected to the network have different effects. The aim of this paper is to present the interoperability between power supply network and PLC network by showing the results of the measurements carried out in the Department of Power Engineering of the Budapest University of Technology and Economics on a one-to-one scale model network considering the problems mentioned above.

articleTitle: Results of Experimental Research of IEMI Effects on a Model of a Typical Computer Network
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper is devoted to an experimental research of immunity of a typical computer network to the action of high voltage pulses injected into information lines and power supply circuits. A model of a computer network, ways of injection of high voltage pulses into a computer network, test equipment, and results of tests are considered.

articleTitle: ATV System Radiated Susceptibility Test
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper focuses on the system radiated susceptibility test performed in the frame of the Automated Transfer Vehicle qualification process. It describes the test specifications and constraints, the preparation process, the test sequence, the results and conclusions.

articleTitle: EMC Studies of Switching Noise and Near-Fields Couplings in Electrical Transport Architectures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper proposes a methodology on a new ElectroMagnetic Compatibility (EMC) multidomain simulation problematic with electronics embedded systems, mixing power components and integrated circuits in common volumes. EMC fields levels as 3D coupling effects, i.e. between on digital Printed Circuit Board (PCB) with Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) pattern and power converter chip (MosPower, Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT)), take place in more and more wide range of frequency, as 10 kHz - 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Engineer Tool for Analyse of EMC System : Power of SPICE Modeling
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In EMC problem, numerous experimental and theoretical methods are available and used by engineer in order to analyse electromagnetic coupling . In this paper, we show that approximate method by circuit modeling can solve most of EMC engineer problems . These tools represent a power and cost effective device for solving problems in EMC system.

articleTitle: Effect of DQ/GIO Data Pattern and Power Delivery Design on EMI in DRAM (Dynamic Random Access Memory)
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents the analysis of DRAM-related EMI depending on DQ/GIO data patterns and power delivery design. DDR2 667 memories are used and the radiated emissions are measured at 1GHz frequency (the 3<sup>rd</sup> harmonic of the clock). Five types of data patterns, which have different magnitudes of EMI-related frequency, are forced to transmit repeatedly and the dependency on radiated emission are measured. As well, three DRAM chips, which have different power delivery design, are tested to see the effect of power delivery design with the data pattern dependency.

articleTitle: Computer Simulations for the Calculation of Q-Factor Related to Electrical Field in a Coach
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The use of mobile phones in coaches and busses may cause problems with the electronic circuitry placed in the vehicle. Resonant patterns may occur, which create locally high field strength. This is characterized by the Q-factor of a coach. In this paper, simulation methods for the calculation and analysis of the resulting electronic field strength distribution and relevant Q factor, are discussed

articleTitle: The Use of Reverberation Chambers in the Quantitative Assessment of the Risk Associated with Installation of Electronic Systems on Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The paper describes the use of reverberation chamber measurements to verify the probability of failure of a vehicle parking sensor corresponds with the theoretical log-normal pdf predicted for current coupled into cables in a reverberant environment. This provides the basis for a quantitative risk assessment system for vehicle electronics.

articleTitle: Investigation in Field of Safety and Reliability of Communication System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: To investigate safety and reliability of communication system different procedures and test equipment have been developed. A plenty of objects have been tested. Some results of investigations in this field are presented below.

articleTitle: IEMI Susceptibilities of Data Links in Local Area Computer Networks; Wlan and Fibre Optics Versus Copper Cable.
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper for the EMC Europe Workshop Paris 2007 presents results from susceptibility testing of commercial off the shelf computer network components. Results for Wireless LAN and Fibre Optic links versus copper cable are compared. For reasons of classification model and brand names are omitted.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Study of the Coupling between a Deterministic Field and a Stochastic System: Application to a Thin Wire over a PEC Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A stochastic method is presented to statistically characterize electromagnetic interactions affected by uncertainties. A stochastically undulating thin-wire over a perfectly conducting ground plane is studied. The aim of this paper is to determine the statistical moments of the voltage induced at the port of this wire by a deterministic incident field. A probabilistic definition of the average and the variance is used. Two methods have been developed to compute these statistical moments: a quadrature method and a perturbation approach.

articleTitle: Analysis of Package Inductance and DQ Driver Strength Dependency on Dram EMI
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes the effect of DRAM- caused power noise on system level EMI. The power noise is regulated by adjusting the package inductance of power delivery nets, DQ driver strength, and the power supply voltage. The package inductances of core power delivery net (VDD/VSS) and the DQ power delivery net (VDDQ/ VSSQ) are controlled by adjusting the number of solder balls on package. Also, the DQ power noise is controlled by adjusting DQ driver strength. The power supply level adjusts to control both core and DQ power noises. In summary, DRAM power noise is closely related to the radiated emission (based on the result of our experiment), and DRAM power noise should be properly controlled to reduce EMI in digital system.

articleTitle: Monte-Carlo Method Applied to a Stochastically Varying Wire above a PEC Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: We investigate the induced voltage due to a wire with stochastic geometry above a perfectly conducting ground plane excited by an incident plane wave. An integral equation method together with the method of moments is applied to account for the full details of the scattering problem. We compute the mean and variance of the induced voltage by means of a Monte-Carlo method. Further, we discuss the convergence rate of the Monte-Carlo method with respect to the ensemble of geometries.

articleTitle: Antenna Coupling Between a Reader and a Mobile Rfid Tag in UHF Short Range / Near Field Application
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The understanding of the near field coupling between RFID UHF label and UHF reader antenna is very important for a good design configuration and optimization of labels and reader antennas. To this aim the near field coupling between labels and reader is investigated in this paper by analytical and numerical approaches. The attention is mainly addressed to the coupling between reader antenna (modeled by loop or circularly polarized antenna) and labels (modeled by loop antenna) in stacked and non-staked positions.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Multicarrier Wireless Systems Affected by a Disturbance using Amplitude Probagility Distribution
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper, the use of amplitude probability distribution (APD) of electromagnetic disturbance is proposed for evaluating a bit error probability after decoding in coded multi-carrier wireless systems. The approximated relational expression that we provide, which is in rather simple form, is verified by the experiments and numerical simulations of an IEEE802.11g model in the presence of repetitive pulse burst.

articleTitle: EMC in Large System Installations
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A new but straight forward approach to characterize the EMC performance of modules and sub-systems to be used in Large System Installations is given, together with an example of simple AC/DC SMPS modules. This characterization will likely lead to the development of new requirements and parameters to be derived for these modules and subsystems used in Large System Installations prior to their installation. The deficiency in the existing measurement procedure of IEC CISPR 16 [1] has been identified and addressed.

articleTitle: Impact of the new EMC Directive on French Railway Infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A revised European EMC directive (2004/108/EC) was published in 2004, in which, for the first time, those supplying fixed installations have a well defined legal obligation to meet the EMC essential requirements. For fixed installations, the mandatory compliance with the essential requirements will come into force as early as July this year (2007). This paper describes the methodology developed by ERA Technology for completing the EMC assurance evidence file for the redevelopment of several railway infrastructures across the UK, such as King's Cross Underground Station in London. This methodology can be applied in the French railway infrastructure for complying with the new EMC directive.

articleTitle: Transposition from Plane Wave System Illumination to Reverberation Chamber Testing using Numerical Simulation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper illustrates the use of numerical simulation to compare induced strains on systems for plane wave illumination and reverberation chamber.

articleTitle: Distributed Reflectometry-Based Diagnosis for Complex Wired Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Reflectometry is a well-known method used for determining the status of electric cables. Applied to wired networks, reflectometry with a single point measurement is not able to detect and to localize faults without ambiguity. This paper presents a method, based on reflectometry, for analyzing the status of any kind of wired network such as field bus or token ring without ambiguity on fault localization. This method uses several digital M-sequence sources connected at each ends of the network under test. The use of different polynomial characteristics, different lengths or different bit rates allow to reduce the source effect in the analysis of the reflectogram.

articleTitle: An Evaluation Method of the Display Image Reconstructed by Electromagnetic Emanation from a Personal Computer
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The display image has been leaked through unintentional electromagnetic emanation from a personal computer. Here we propose an evaluation method of the leaked image. The leaked image can be reconstructed by means of a signal averaging technique and a binary recording technique by a threshold value. The evaluation method makes use of the overlap rate between the display image and the leaked image. The processing procedure is shown to decide uniquely the overlap rate. Using this procedure, we demonstrate that the leaked image with characters is reconstructed and evaluated as the overlap rate 90[%] or more. Our proposed method can evaluate uniquely the information leakage of a display image through electromagnetic emanation from a personal computer.

articleTitle: Study of Functional Behavior of an Electronic System Placed in Hostile Electromagnetic Environment
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper, we present the functional behavior of an electronic system placed in hostile electromagnetic environment. In this study, we try to understand the mechanisms of failures of an electronic system, for which one knows his architecture. One of the objectives of this study is to try to predict a functional behavior of the system when it is subjected to a given electromagnetic environment. To undertake this study, we must on the one hand, well to control the system to be studied, on the aspects hardware and software, and on the other hand, we must also know the electromagnetic environment in which the system will be placed.

articleTitle: Modelling of Components and Circuits up to 3 GHz
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Parasitic effects in electronic circuits become very important when high frequencies are used. In this paper, several passive components are measured in the frequency range from 30 kHz to 3 GHz and suitable models are obtained for them. Then, a high-pass filter has been designed and implemented using those components. After measuring the final circuit, some additional parasitic mutual couplings have been observed and modelled.

articleTitle: Antenna Size Sensitivity on the Statistic of Received Power Measurements in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper introduces a new perception in the analysis of distribution functions for the received power in a reverberation chamber (RC). As part of an ideal RC, the theoretical model assumes that the power received at an antenna is distributed as an exponential function above the lowest usable frequency (LUF) of the cavity. This paper provides experimental results in order to highlight the effect of the size of the antenna over the probability density function of measurements. Over the LUF, when the exponential distribution doesn't fit well the measurements, the Weibull function with two parameters presents better performances. The results presented here are obtained following an intensive and rigorous statistical analysis on a large collection of data, using high power goodness of fit (GOF) tests.

articleTitle: Practice Experience on Electromagnetic Fields Measurements in the Urban Environment with Respect to Icnirp-98 Standard
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper intends to address the characterizing of electromagnetic environments actually present in urban homes in Madrid, with respect to the assessment for potential safe use of home telemedicine systems. Data is scarce on electromagnetic radiation in the home environment. Field studies have been performed with a radiation monitor in accordance with ICNIRP-98. Results from these studies reveals that baseline levels are within the safety margin in accordance with the current standard, it appear to remain quite stable over time and irrespective of the location in the city. However, the presence of relative high peaks or burst of radiated signals in the proximity of household equipment have been observed.

articleTitle: Upper and Lower Bounds Estimation of the Response of Indoor Power Line Communication Systems Characterized by Cyclostationary Loads
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper we focus our attention on the channel variation of indoor powerline channels caused by the presence of nonlinear loads. The nonlinear behavior of some electrical devices (with respect to the mains voltages) produces short time variations synchronous to the mains. The goal of our investigation is to obtain estimates of the upper and lower bounds of the channel's response both in the time and in the frequency domain in such situation. Nonlinearities are modeled in the frequency domain as the sum of a nominal value impedance and a number of elementary pulse shaped terms with uncertain weights. The indoor power line channel is modeled in the wavelet domain and a sensitivity analysis with respect to the weights is performed by the adjoint circuit method. The proposed method allows a fast and accurate evaluation of the bounds of the response of the channel avoiding time consuming Montecarlo simulations.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating Fependence of Disturbance APD on Measurement Frequency
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: To estimate the impact of electromagnetic disturbance on multi-carrier wireless systems, a method for converting an amplitude probability distribution (APD) of disturbance from a measured frequency to another frequency is presented. The conversion uses two parameters, the receiver noise power of the APD measuring equipment and a scale factor that can be estimated by a measured disturbance spectrum. The method is based on an assumption that difference in the measurement frequency affects only the relative scale of the amplitude probability distribution of disturbance, and is applicable to practically important disturbances such as 1) continuous or pulse-modulated wideband Gaussian noise, 2) disturbance with a much narrower bandwidth than receiver bandwidth B, and 3) repetitive short pulses with similar waveforms with an interval much longer than 1/B. The validity of the proposed method is demonstrated by measurements of actual disturbances.

articleTitle: Mask Based Mobility Model a 2-D Outdoor 3-D Indoor Mobility Model
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a new mobility model: the Mask Based Mobility Model (MBMM). This model uses Markov chains for human displacement simulations. After a brief overview of existing mobility models the MBMM is presented in details showing its 2D and 3D aspects that enables it to handle outdoor and indoor displacement case studies. Simulations of 2D and 3D case studies are then given. Finally, a general conclusion that summarizes the new models' aspects is presented.

articleTitle: Broadband Indoor PLC: Comparison of Different Models for Simulating Impulsive Noise
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Two of the most critical points in implementing PLC (Power Line Communication) technology are the wide variability of the propagation channel and the presence of impulsive noise. In this paper, we focus exclusively on the characterization and modelling of impulsive noise, whose random character and strong power spectral density can seriously disturb link performance, particularly in the case of high-speed transmissions. The resulting noise model could be implemented in a simulation tool, thus allowing the channel coding to be optimized.

articleTitle: Characterisation and Impact of the Microwave Ovens over a Wi-Fi System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The growth of wireless communications systems in the home application and their evolution, especially their lower sensibility level, drive to new cohabitation issues with domestic equipments. Personal Computers and microwave ovens are often taken into considerations. This article deals with the microwave ovens and two of their characteristics: one is the relation between the duty cycle of the oven and the cooking power and the other is the interference over the WiFi equipments. It is shown that the cooking power do not impact the maximum power level but only the duty cycle of emission of this noise. It is also shown that, for a distance of 1 meter, all the channels are impacted, the worst case was with the shutdown of the link.

articleTitle: Efficient Reduction of the Crosstalk between two Coupled Microstrip Lines using Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper, we show how metamaterials can be used to reduce the crosstalk between the strips of coupled microstriplines. The coupling/crosstalk between regular coplanar microstriplines can be undesirable in printed circuits. The employment of metamaterials with a negative real part of the permittivity is able to decrease the coupling values, while keeping the profile of the structure very low. A quasi-static model of the structure is developed and physical insights on the operation of the proposed components and on the role of the metamaterial loading are also given. Finally numerical results are shown for the proposed layout.

articleTitle: On Cancelling Crosstalk by Transmitting Signals Following a Particular Combination of Modes
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a method of crosstalk reduction in a four conductor telecommunication cable composed of two twisted pairs. An electromagnetic and topologic code is implemented to simulate the multi conductor transmission line when injecting the different signals following a particular combination of modes. Thus, the far end crosstalk voltage is determined. With such a method, it appears that is possible to decrease crosstalk on the line.

articleTitle: Inductive Interference Mitigation on Wayside Double Track Territory
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: High voltage transmission lines and low voltage distribution lines often share a corridor with railroads. The load currents in these lines radiate an electric field that induces voltages and currents in the rails, which are connected by cables to the signal system electronics. These voltages and currents can exceed 100 V and 100 A and seriously affect the signal systems. One way to mitigate severe inductive interference problems is to apply impedance bonds across the insulated joints. In double track territory, both tracks require impedance bonds with earth grounds. These grounds need to be independent in order to maintain broken rail detection capability. In this paper, we present experimental and analytic results for mitigating a 25 km long corridor having severe interference levels, focusing on methods of obtaining low resistance earth grounds and application of these grounds in double track territory in such a way to maintain broken rail detection capability

articleTitle: The new EMC Directive and its Impact on the Railway Industry
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The requirements of the new EMC Directive 2004/108/EC will apply from 20<sup>th</sup> July 2007 with a two-year transition period until July 2009. The new Directive applies to ‘equipment’ and splits these into two categories. “apparatus” and “fixed installations”. and applies different compliance requirements to each.

articleTitle: Effect of Structure and Materials of Building on Electromagnetic Fields Generated by Indoor Power Line Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Power line communications (PLC) allow transmission of data over power lines. A serious matter of the PLC is a radiation caused by common-mode signal current flowing along the power lines, which may cause interference with radio systems in HF band. The common-mode radiation by power lines that are installed in a building leaks outside the building. In this report, the electromagnetic-field attenuations by buildings are numerically analyzed by using the finite- integration (FI) method.

articleTitle: The Scenario of Intentionally Radiated Electromagnetic Interference to Railway Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The future electrical railway system relies heavily on wireless control of and communication with the trains. This paper investigates the threat of HPM interference radiated towards the GSM-R antennas of the communication systems of the railway. Threshold levels of the communication system are used to calculate the minimum bore-sight distance for realistic HPM sources for causing permanent damage to the system.

articleTitle: Characterisation of the EM Noise inside Machines Related to Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The use of short range wireless systems in industrial environments increases enormous due to the evolution of different data-communication technologies. Many of these wireless communication systems use the unlicensed Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) frequency bands. The increased use of these frequency bands increases also the interference sensitivity of the systems. This makes it difficult to predict a system will work properly in industrial environments without characterizing these environments. The characterization of an industrial environment depends not only on the interference pattern. Many mechanical and electromagnetic effects determine also the behaviour of wireless communication systems. This paper discusses some parameters which should be taken care of in the characterization of an industrial environment.

articleTitle: On Measuring the Transfer Function that Correlates GTEM Cell to Oats Emission Measurements
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Emission measurements, normally done under OATS conditions, can be carried out in a GTEM cell using formulas that correlate those two techniques. Although theoretically the field inside the cell can be described analytically, in reality due to the improper behavior of the GTEM cell sometimes the homogeneity is not quite given. This is shown in measurements with a special scanner that moves a sensor inside the cell measuring the E-field. Comparison is made with the calculated field inside the cell and sources of possible measurement errors are pointed out.

articleTitle: Radiated Emission from Personal Computers - A Safety Risk for GPS Receivers?
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The development towards faster data buses and processors in personal computers has lead to a significant contribution of radiated emission in the present frequency bands for the Global Positioning System (GPS). In this paper we show that the radiated emission from modern personal computers seriously can affect the ability of GPS receivers to acquire the satellite signals. This radiated emission can therefore be a safety risk for GPS receivers and has to be considered in system development of applications that are dependent on GPS services.

articleTitle: Assessement of Code Rate Effects on DVB-T Systems Perfomance in the Presence of Interference
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Effects of code rate on the performance of Digital Video Broadcasting-Terrestrial (DVB-T) systems in the presence of in-channel interference are here assessed. In particular, major parameters at physical and application layers are considered, and two types of interfering phenomena are enlisted: Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) and impulsive interference. The purpose is to deduce helpful information for optimizing the choice of code rate in some real-life configurations, thus allowing broadcasters and system designers to gain low bit error rate and high throughput. A number of experiments are carried out upon the varying of code rate and other system parameters, and the obtained results are shown. A proper testbed including a real DVB-T platform is arranged, and a cross-layer measurement approach is exploited.

articleTitle: Overview of EMC Issues in the Perspective of the Future Aeronautical Communication System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a description of a possible new aeronautical digital radiocommunication system and the various configurations for studying the associated electromagnetic compatibility problems. In this field, some studies have already been published by EUROCONTROL or the US Federal Aviation Administration. Nevertheless, the originality of this work is to describe the possible radio systems and to try to assess some of the electromagnetic compatibility issues associated to any new radio aeronautical system, as EMC is one of the major aspects of the design of the future aeronautical communication system.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Scattering Parameter Measurement of Electronic Equipment with Conducted Emissions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents two new measurement methods useful to obtain a better characterization of the input impedance of electronic equipment connected to the power line. This characterization is performed using a three-impedance pi-model network, which is obtained from an S-parameter measurement of the equipment. Both methods proposed in this paper improve the accuracy of S-parameter measurements, and consequently yield more accurate equivalent models. The knowledge of these models is very useful to design and/or to choose the most suitable power-line filter, since they allow an accurate prediction of the filter attenuation in common and differential modes. These new techniques are experimentally tested using real measurements.

articleTitle: Coupling Mom and PEEC Methods with Kron's Transformation for EMC Study of Embedded Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper is dealing with a new approach for using coupling between the Moments Method (MoM) and the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) method with the Kron's transformation to deal with calculating coupling among separate structures on embedded systems. The PEEC method is used to study the coupling at the level of the low-size systems with fine details such as the multi-layers printed circuits boards. However, The Moments method is used for calculation of the coupling between the distant parts with metallic structures and apertures. The Kron's method makes possible to transform the matrix of coupling into reduced matrix in order to make it easy-handled, and makes it possible to calculate the coupling between the two structures. This methodology is applied to a simple structure constituted by two square circuits. The obtained results are validated with experimental measurements.

articleTitle: “Equivalent Cable Bundle Method” : A Suitable Approach for the Evaluation of Coupling on Automotive Cable Harnesses
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents the so-called “Equivalent Cable Bundle Method” performed for the calculation of common mode (CM) currents induced on cable bundles by a disturbing electromagnetic (EM) wave over a large frequency range. Indeed, in EMC domain, it is well known that the cables which link the different devices located inside a complex system such as cars, trains or aircrafts play an important role in the susceptibility level and in the radiation of the entire system. Due to the increasing of the spectrum of disturbing sources over the last years, the high frequency assessment of the coupling of a disturbing EM wave on a cable network becomes of great importance. The purpose of the method proposed is to reduce the complexity of a cable structure, under some assumptions we will present, in order to reduce consequently the computation time necessary to perform a 3D numerical calculation at “high frequencies”. We first present the theoretical basis of the method and second the numerical and experimental validations performed on prototypal cable bundles or harnesses in order to illustrate the capability and the advantages of the method.

articleTitle: EMI Radiations Emitted by Power Lines of PWM Converters in Airplane Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The increasing use of converters and electromechanical actuators in airplane requires the check of the electromagnetic compatibility at the design step of such new electrical systems. Actuators and converters are linked by variable length power cable which may radiate. So, in order to estimate the magnetic field emitted by a power wire, we propose to model the wire and to measure the voltage source and the load impedance. The magnetic field is estimated with the transmission line theory and the method of image.

articleTitle: Test for Interdependency of Immunity on Automotive Electronic Sub-Assemblies (ESA's)
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The objective of this paper is to give a precise method to validate Automotive Electronic sub-assemblies (ESA) for Radiated Immunity test. Due to rapid growth in automotive electronics technology, number of electronic components also increased simultaneously. All component operation and safety is dependent on the reliable functioning of complex control and monitoring systems. General practices of OEM are, by sticking to the regulations and Standards, for doing Radiated immunity test on ESA. But this is not the proper solution to analyze the compatibility of ESA in such an environment, which can creates problem during vehicle level validation. To avoid these kinds of discrepancies & difficulties during vehicle validation, ESA should be validated in system level. Presently, the automotive industry has the practice of conducting immunity test at ESA level (as per the standard) during new development, which will usually meet the test requirement. But problem occurs during vehicle level validation because the issues are not captured in ESA testing. The system level validation, which can simulate the vehicle conditions, is advisable for Radiated Immunity test for ESA. To evaluate the interdependency of immunity between the electronic aggregates, it is advisable to connect them along with related vehicle aggregates during the radiated immunity test.

articleTitle: Propagation of PLC Signals through Circuit Breakers
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: PLC signal propagation is affected by all the elements present in a single-phase power-line network, generating attenuation, frequency selectivity on the channel and mode conversion between differential and common modes. It is therefore necessary to characterize all the elements in the network to gain understanding about the processes which lead to PLC signal propagation degradation. In this paper, an analysis of the transfer characteristics of several circuit breakers is performed. Their attenuation to differential mode and common mode is measured, as well as their mode conversion from differential mode to common mode, and conversely. Finally, generic conclusions are drawn from the measurements performed.

articleTitle: Power Converters Conducted Emissions and EMI Filtering
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with conducted emissions in power converters. Based on multi physical and multi scale approach, a topological method worked out by G.Kron is used, first, in time domain to keep topological information such as switches commutations and, secondly, in frequency domain for a more efficient computation of EMC (Electro-Magnetic Compatibility) results thanks to equivalent sources. The waveforms estimation followed by the filter modelling in frequency domain make possible to optimize the EMI (Electro-Magnetic Interferences) filtering at the design stage. The computations are realized under Scilab free mathematical tool.

articleTitle: Estimating the Total Radiated Power of a Wire & Shielded Box Structure from Common-Mode Current Measurement
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: An EMI antenna comprised of a shielded enclosure and wiring harness is used in this paper to model the emission characteristics of a automotive electronic component. The mode-stirring reverberation chamber and EMI antenna was modeled as a two-port network. An empirical transfer function derived from the measurement of S parameters is able to correlate the total radiated power measured in MSRC and the bench-top common-mode-current measurement.

articleTitle: Video Analysis - Spectral Analysis of Radiated Emissions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: During measurements of radiated emissions in situ or on an OATS we frequently have to face the problem, that it is impossible to assess if detected interference signals are related to the DUT or to other sources. The spectral analysis of the video output (the envelope of the detected signal) of the measuring receiver enables us to distinguish between interference signals of interest (associated to the DUT) and spurious signals from other sources. The whole procedure, along with corresponding measurements and potential benefits are presented.

articleTitle: Time Domain Analysis of Multiconductor Shielded Cables using MNA Methode: Circuit Model
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A circuit model is developed for the evaluation in frequency and time domain, of voltages at the terminals of a multiconductors shielded cable. The proposed macromodel circuit do not need the usual subdivision of the circuits in elementary cells, it is valid in both frequency and time domain and is based on the exact solution of the equations transmission line model, and takes into account the presence of both transfer impedance and admittance. This model can be easily inserted in circuit analysis software like SPICE. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the validity of proposed model.

articleTitle: Modeling the Response of Spatially Inhomogeneous Communciation and Sensor Networks against IEMI using Percolation Theory
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper addresses the survivability of spatially inhomogeneous ad-hoc large communication and/or sensor systems when they are attacked by Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI). The proposed metric for survivability is the network's ability to remain radio-frequency connected over its initial area with the surviving fraction of nodes—does a network spanning cluster exist? We address this problem by extending the method of position-space renormalization to the inhomogeneous network regime.

articleTitle: The “Power Integrity View” of PCB Design Managing Power Distribution System Design & Analysis
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The overall performance and the EMC behavior of electronic equipment is not only determined by the design of the circuitry and the geometry of the layout, but also by the power supply system. Noise voltages on the power/ground system, caused by the fast switching currents of integrated circuits (ICs), can lead to significant electromagnetic emissions. In order to evaluate these noise voltages on power distribution systems efficiently, a fast and sufficient accurate algorithm is able to evaluate the PDS impedance, including all resonances, the noise voltage and, subsequently, for the radiated emission by the power supply system.. Herefore all relevant system components (i.e. the ICs) have to be characterized in an appropriate manner, including the die itself as well as the package, therefore a deep integration within a PCB CAD environment is mandatory.

articleTitle: On the Use of Wireless Communication Systems on Ships
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Replacing cables by wireless communication systems is a well known task in modern industry and home use. Also on modern ships this replacement can be applied. Different aspects of replacing cables by wireless communication systems on ships are presented. Measurements of the electromagnetic spectrum on a ship have been performed to achieve an overview of possible interferer in the environment ship. It is shown that using wireless communication systems on the environment ship is generally possible.

articleTitle: Magnetic Cartography and Susceptibility of Logic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper focuses on magnetic field cartography and susceptibility of logic circuits, up to 20 GHz frequency range. Logic gates are placed upon three different printed boards, single or double sided. Both z and x-y magnetic radiated field components are measured in order to establish field cartographies. The most radiating zones are then chosen as injection points for magnetic aggression. It is shown that a parasitic signal superimposes itself on the output signal of the gates under test. Characteristics of the parasitic signal differ versus frequency and printed board type.

articleTitle: Sensor Network for Detection and Localization of Mobile Phones Aboard Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Detection and localization of mobile phones aboard aircrafts is an important safety issue because the electromagnetic interference generated by such devices can seriously affect the airplane electronic instruments especially during the critical phases of take off and landing. In this paper a discovery and localization procedure based on a sensor network is described as a practical solution for modern aircrafts. Its performance is also analyzed for some different number of nodes.

articleTitle: Electric Dipole for Electric Radiated Field Susceptibility Test
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Nowadays, all electronic systems are subjected to various electromagnetic disturbances. A lot of works on radiated field's susceptibility test were performed on magnetic disturbances using a magnetic loop probe. This paper deals with electric radiated field disturbance using an electric dipole (see figure 1), this one had largely been studied but generally as a detector. We propose to evidence and characterize the interest of such a probe to allow inducing failure in a digital CMOS circuit behaviour.

articleTitle: FDTD Analysis of the Distribution of a Transient Field inside a Car
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The present article studies the behavior of a transient electromagnetic impulse produced inside a car through numerical computation by using the Finite Differences Time Domain (FDTD) method. Electric field measurements taken in different places within the vehicle were compared to the results of the numerical simulation when settings in the grid sampling were changed. We concluded that it is possible to make studies in time domain with sufficient reliability and reduced computation resources.

articleTitle: Conditions of Electromagnetic Compatibility of Narrowband and Ultrawideband Radio Equipment: A Method of Calculation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper we present a method for calculating the conditions necessary for elimination of interference between radio equipment when the transmitter bandwidth differs essentially from the receiver bandwidth. The method can be used for providing electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) of narrowband and ultrawideband radio equipment. Such radio equipment is finding increased usage in modern radio communication and control systems.

articleTitle: Coexistence between VDSL2 Broadband Equipments and Amateur Radio
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Customer demand and new opportunities for network operators require that Internet access allows higher data flows. Today's, broadband connections to the customer is mainly realized with a more than 10 years old technology called Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL). Although there has been a fear that this technology would completely render an important part of the frequency spectrum completely unusable, experience has shown that very few interference cases were reported. The newer technology, which is currently installed, is called Very high speed Digital Subscriber Line (VDSL2). Faster data transfers are achieved by using a frequency band about 10 times wider than ADSL. This paper presents key aspects of the newer technology and its potential influence on amateur radio services.

articleTitle: Measurement & Modelling Investigations INTO Practical Cable Separations in an Urban Metro Environment
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Typical Cable Management System (CMS) design uses multi-compartment metallic trunking with low voltage power and communications/data cables running in adjacent compartments. In many commercial deployments no other physical separation distance between power and communications cables is implemented, the assumption being that the trunking provides electromagnetic shielding to limit the level of voltage coupling between cables. However, the trunking used is not designed specifically for Electro-Magnetic Compatibility (EMC) and has unknown shielding properties. This study has examined whether this arrangement will be adequate for the control of induced voltages in the context of a complex urban metro environment.

articleTitle: Characterization of the Mains Network for PLC Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The standardization process for broadband over powerline (BPL, PLC) is still going on. This topic is getting very important again due to high market penetration of DSL accesses. Newly the customer must make a choice between DSL-routers with an integrated WLAN or an in-house PLC modem. This will increase the number of installed PLC devices and could result in a higher number of harmful interference between the modem as a noise source and a short wave radio receiver as the victim. This paper will give the motivation for the development of the new measurement procedure that is in discussion in CISPR [1-3]. Beside the definition of different symmetry and decoupling factors the latest improvements of the measurement setup (obtained in the COST286 JTA2) will be presented. Measurement results for the different factors will be shown and compared.

articleTitle: SoC Prototyping Environment for Electromagnetic Immunity Measurements
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: We present a configurable standard environment for electromagnetic (EM) immunity measurement of prototype system-on-chip (SoC). The environment is composed of two boards compliant with the 62.132-2 and 62.132-4 IEC Std Parts, being conceived for radiated and conducted measurements, respectively. The SoC under test can be prototyped on two types of ICs: two FPGAs and a microcontroller. Practical experiments have been carried out. The obtained results demonstrate the utility and benefits from using the proposed platform to estimate in an early stage of the design process the behavior of embedded systems operating in EM environment.

articleTitle: E-Field Probe Calibration vs Antenna Calibration in MSRC
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Currently, the calibration of a reverberating chamber is achieved by E-field probe in the working volume in order to determine the limits for which the environment can be regarded as uniform and isotropic. Several formulations to obtain the field from power measurement exist through standards DO160 and IEC 61000-4-21. This document presents several ways of comparison between the calibration by E-field probe and antenna.

articleTitle: EMC Aspects of Development of Data Bus Systems in Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with EMC of data buses and how it can be handled in the vehicle development process. A method for fast simulations of vehicle data buses is presented. The numerical method including the analysis of measurement data for characterizing the bus driver circuits can handle harmonics up to several hundred MHz. This is sufficient for the new generation of fast data busses that now are introduced in vehicles. The high computational speed relies on the fact that common mode radiation from a twisted pair is similar to that from two parallel wires.

articleTitle: Reverberation Chambers for Testing Performances of Mobile Communication systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: If reverberation chambers have been used since many years in the framework of electromagnetic compatibility, they are nowadays also used to characterize and to test wireless channels. In this paper, several parameters of wireless channels are shown to be easily obtained inside a reverberation chamber. The case of a testbed composed of two reverberation chambers is also discussed.

articleTitle: Link Rapid I/O Transceiver-NIU: Signal Integrity Analysis & Measures
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: • Scope of this task is to carry out the analysis of signal integrity and measures on Bread Board, for a Line Rapid I/O connected among different modules.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Information Leakage from PC Display using Suggested Image
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: To evaluate information leakage from a PC display and to determine whether the electromagnetic disturbance contains information or not, we need to reconstruct the display image of the measured disturbance using a special receiver. However, not all test facilities have such a receiver. Therefore, we propose an evaluation method that uses two spectrum analyzers commonly used for EMI measurement. We evaluated information that leaks from a PC display using several images, and selected the best image for evaluating electromagnetic disturbance.

articleTitle: On the Use of the Hatfield Technique for EM Qualification of Large Aircrafts
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The principle of low level transfer functions measurements according to the “Hatfield” technique is given. Measurements performed on a van inside a regular metallic hall illustrate the potentialities of this technique.

articleTitle: Finite Volume Models for Reverberation Chamber Loaded with a Generic Automotive Device
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with numerical modeling of a Mode Stirred Reverberation Chamber (MSRC). Advantages and difficulties related to simulations in time/frequency domains in MSRC are underlined. Most commonly spread, FDTD techniques suffer from a lack of flexibility to completely describe complex geometrical models. On the contrary, Finite Volume (FV) methods allow straightforward design of realistic MSRC devices. Predicted FV numerical results are compared with those obtained by FD simulations on practical cases involving MSRC in time domain.

articleTitle: The Railcom Project Electromagnetic Compatibility between Rolling Stock and Rail-Infrastructure Encouraging European Interoperability7
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Presently railway product designers and manufacturers are faced with a complex mixture of legacy, train detection and communication systems. New communication technologies and products are appearing at a rapid rate with applications in the railway industry being targeted. The European Commission has attempted to simplify the market place through the development of Trans-European Networks and their associated access requirements, Technical Specifications for Interoperability (TSI's). “Electromagnetic compatibility between rolling stock and rail-infrastructure encouraging European interoperability” (RAILCOM) addresses this domain by focussing on improvements of two specific railway vehicle-infrastructure interfaces on the TEN railway network: • Compatibility between train detection systems (infrastructure) and electromagnetic interference from railway vehicles; • Electromagnetic compatibility of railway communication systems between vehicles, infrastructure, employees and passengers. In the topic of electromagnetic compatibility there has been difficulty in establishing clear design requirements and acceptance techniques. Through RAILCOM the partners wish to help support this issue by the definition of new design parameters, manufacturing processes and particularly acceptance procedures for the compatibility of railway rolling stock with train detection systems and new railway communication systems. The use of such procedures will help smooth the introduction and ensure immunity of these new communication interfaces to electromagnetic noise with guarantees of system interoperability across Europe. For both interfaces the establishment of electromagnetic limits and acceptance procedures at a European level will greatly assist the interoperability of rolling stock for both passengers and freight transportation across borders.

articleTitle: Simulation of A 5.8GHz Antenna Integrated INTO a Vehicle for Automotive DSRC Applications
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a simulation study of a 5.8GHz patch antenna integrated into a vehicle for Dedicated Short Range Communication applications (DSRC). The DSRC deals with car-to-car and car-to-infrastructure communications and will permit to improve road transport by using information and communication technologies. This study provides simulation results validated by measurements that enable to assess the effects of car structures on radiation patterns.

articleTitle: Large Scale FDTD Analysis for Implantable Cardiac Pacemaker EMI due to Mobile Radios in Train Carriages of Complicated Situations
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The purpose of this study is to estimate electromagnetic interference on implantable cardiac pacemaker from mobile radios used in train carriages based upon the precise numerical analysis considering the realistic and complex situations wherein humans occupy. We have reported that pacemaker malfunction due to cellular radios did not occur even if five passengers use the radios simultaneously at the maximum level. In this paper, more complicated and realistic situations in the cases where more cellular phone users and passengers exist in the carriage are examined. Our study shows that the effects of losses due to the human body should not be disregarded. As a result, it is shown that any electromagnetic fields excited by cellular phones might not affect implantable cardiac pacemakers except in the vicinity of the transmitting cellular phones.

articleTitle: On the Use of EMC Compliance Test Results to Demonstrate EMF Compliance
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Both for Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) and for human exposure to electromagnetic fields (EMF), limits are set to the emission of electromagnetic fields of electronic products. This paper analyzes whether results of EMC emission measurements can be used to demonstrate compliance with EMF requirements. For the investigated products without intended radiators this is indeed the case. However, additional EMF assessments remain necessary for frequency ranges that are not covered by the EMC measurements.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Information Leakage from PC Display by the Frequency Component of the Vertical SYNC Signal
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: To evaluate electromagnetic disturbance that contains information leaked from a PC display, we need to use a special receiver to reconstruct the displayed image. We propose a way of evaluating electromagnetic disturbance that contains information without the need to reconstruct a displayed image. Our proposed method is to evaluate on the basis of the level difference of the vertical sync signal between the maximum value and the minimum value. First, we measure the level difference of electromagnetic disturbance in the time-domain. Then, we use this method to measure the frequency-domain. We are thus able to use this method to evaluate whether electromagnetic disturbance contains information or not.

articleTitle: Random Graphs and Percolation Theory Applied to Survivability of AD-HOC Wireless Communication and Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: New theoretical principals based on random graph theory and percolation theory are proposed for evaluating the resilience of large ad-hoc communication and sensor networks against naturally caused and Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI). A comparison of survivable communications based on Cold War principals and current networks is rendered. A key element of our proposed theory is the concept of survivability based on the emergence of a network spanning cluster and its relationship to the information rate for an individual node and overall network capacity.

articleTitle: Development of an Integrated EMC Information Management System for Automotive Application
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes the framework of an EMC Information Management System (EMCIMS) that incorporated EMC design principal and support ed the EMC management in component/subsystem product development in automotive industry. The EMCIMS is an environment to allow open sharing and comparison of measurement data and simulation data, enhance collective EMC knowledge building.

articleTitle: Producing an EMC Safety Case for the Channel Tunnel Rail Link
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper describes the processes and methodology used to produce an EMC Safety Case for the Channel Tunnel Rail Link. Examples are presented of identified EMC issues and the processes used to resolve them.

articleTitle: Project of Embedded System Operating with Wireless/Wired Interfaces for the Implementation of GSM/UMTS Sensor Network in Aeronautic Environment
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper a monitoring and alarming automated system to detect mobile phone emissions on airplanes is proposed. Based on TCP/IP protocols, we proposed a GSM/UMTS and environmental sensor network using Rabbit microprocessors. We developed a prototype that detects the presence of active GSM/UMTS terminals with the possibility of viewing and managing the retrieved information; this is possible because a web interface based on open source technologies (MySQL, PHP, Apache) was created. At the same time the system can integrate easy functions for monitoring further on-board parameters like temperature, humidity and vibrations.

articleTitle: Powerline Communication In-Vehicle Car Networking
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper deals with power line communication techniques for high data rate in automotive environnement. In order to reduce the total amount of cables and EMC, a potential solution is power line communications (PLC), using multi-carrier modulation. This technique offers both high data rate and good adequacy with channel properties. In the final paper, measurements of noises and PLC techniques will be presented in the automotive environment.

articleTitle: Time Domain Modeling of Integrated Circuit Packages on Massively Parallel Computers
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The time domain electromagnetic field simulation based on massive parallelization is proposed as a tool for the signal integrity analysis of complex IC packages. The simulations are based on a specialized domain partitioning method which allows for highly balanced parallel computations. As a real- world example the analysis of a large computer chip spreader is performed. Numerical results including signal wave forms and delay times are given.

articleTitle: Characterisation of the Electromagnetic Disturbances Received by GSM-R Antennas in Usual Railway Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: To insure the interoperability of the european trains, the communication systems between the trains and the control centers have to be harmonized over the European Railway Network. In this context, the Global System for Mobiles-Railways (GSM-R) will progressively equip all the trains for transmissions of voice and data between the vehicles and the infrastructures. This system has to be able to bear the electromagnetic disturbances produced on board trains to insure the transmission of the information. However, the current standardised methods to characterize electromagnetic noise in railway environment are not convenient for this application. This paper compares different methods, tested in the framework of the RAILCOM project, to characterize the electromagnetic noise received by GSM-R antennas and analyzes the disturbance characteristics which can impact the reliability of the GSM-R system.

articleTitle: A New Single-Ended I/O for Low EME Binary Data Link
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The paper describes a new technique to establish binary links between integrated circuits. Starting from the operation of common single-ended input/output (I/O) circuits, which are widely used as building blocks of microprocessors, DSPs and semiconductor memories, the paper describes a new output buffer and its respective receiver, that communicates each other by means of electric charge pulses. Through this new communication method and using the related input and output circuits, power consumption and signal integrity issues as well as electromagnetic emission of single-ended I/Os can be significantly reduced.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Electromagnetic Absorbing Screens Including Metamaterials for Electromagnetic Interference Suppression
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: An optimization tool based on genetic algorithms is developed in order to design electrically thin absorbing screens including metamaterials for electromagnetic interference suppression. The optimization procedure is fully detailed and some design solutions of sub-wavelength screens are proposed.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of WLAN Interference Effects on IEEE 802.15.4 Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Interference effects of Wireless Local Area Networks (WLANs) on Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are here investigated. In particular, the performance of a IEEE 802.15.4 WSN upon the varying of some meaningful parameters and in the presence of a near operating IEEE 802.11b WLAN is analyzed. The purpose is to deduce helpful information for network designers, users and standardization committees for optimizing the performance and reliability of a IEEE 802.15.4 WSN when operating in the presence of an interfering WLAN. Experiments are conducted through a proper test system, and different WSN configurations are considered.

articleTitle: Security of Aircraft in the Future European Environment “SAFEE”
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Presented work is undertaken in the frame of the on course “SAFEE” EUROPEAN Integrated Project of the 6th European Framework Program. This is a large project designed to restore full confidence in the air transport industry, constructing an advanced aircraft security system designed to prevent on-board threats. To reach this objective SAFEE deals with onboard threat detection, studying an integrated threat detection system based on multiple sensor information. Among project's objectives is the protection of voice and data communications which are daily used for exploitation of aircraft in a hostile fashion that may lead to a dramatic situation like direct or indirect control of the aircraft by hijackers or use of false data that can endanger the flight safety. Characterization of Electromagnetic threats coupling with on-board antennas is the presented work. This is carried out taking into account different front door threats scenarios and looking for interference results by modeling Electromagnetic intrusive signals.

articleTitle: An Intelligent CG Lightning Location System, using Field Radiations from Return Stroke Channels
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Generation of national standard practice codes for protection against lightning discharge requires intelligent systems to measure, detect, locate, and identify lightning activities. Cloud-to- ground (CG) lightning is the most dangerous type of lightning and is widely studied in the optimal design of lightning protection systems. This paper describes the development of an intelligent lightning location system, capable of rejecting unwanted transient signals such as switching signals, cloud-to-cloud lightning signals, etc. The system is a network of three lightning detection stations located at the vertices of a triangle covering Tehran province, Iran.

articleTitle: In-Situ Measurements of Radiated Emission on Large Industrial Apparatus
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: In this paper, some meaningful issues concerning the measurement of radiated emissions generated by large apparatus for heavy industrial applications are discussed. The study initiated to define practical hints for the mitigation of EMC problems associated to large dimensions machines, and led back to investigate about useful methods for radiated emissions measurement, other than the Open Area Test Sites (OATS). The configuration analyzed represents a “worst case” situation for the apparatus both for emission and immunity.

articleTitle: Field Levels Excited within and in the Neighborhood of a Mobile Vehicle Employed for Radio Communications in Crisis Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A combined UTD/FDTD technique is adopted to evaluate the electromagnetic field levels excited within and around a vehicle integrating a transceiver useful to guarantee the radio link in crisis scenarios. A particular emphasis is devoted to the analysis of the effects caused by the vehicle on the radiation diagram of the antenna, as well as to the electromagnetic field distribution excited within the considered vehicle. The disturbance levels induced along transmission lines modeling sensitive electronic equipment located in the nearby of the vehicle are also evaluated.

articleTitle: Cable Modelling for Common Mode Interference Estimation in Embedded Power Electronics Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Two different methods for calculating power cable impedances are introduced and compared. The knowledge of these impedances is needed in order to estimate common mode currents in power systems like a three phase inverter supplying an AC motor. The first part is dedicated to the wire geometries and characteristics of electrical cable used in power systems. In the second part, the first method, based on thin wire approximation and analytical formulation, and the second method, based on P.E.E.C. calculation are presented. The per-unit-length parameters and the cable impedance versus frequency computed using these methods are then discussed.

articleTitle: Compatibility between Rolling Stock, Signalling Systems, and Traction Power Supply Systems; A Study for Portuguese Railways
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A railway system is a transport system on which high requirements are imposed with respect to reliability and safety. A railway system consists of a large number of subsystems, with mutual interactions, such as: Traction Power Supply Systems, Signalling Systems; Telecommunication Systems and Rolling Stock These systems are owned by various parties such as train operating companies and infrastructure managers, which increases the complexity. This leads to a large distributed system, for which it not only must be proven that electromagnetic compatibility exists between all systems, but at the same time the reliability, safety and availability must be at a high level. Due to the increasing use of power electronics in rolling stock, the emissions of harmonic currents of the rolling stock is increasing, not only in magnitude, but also higher frequencies are present. As the Eigen frequencies of the Traction Power Supply System are relatively low the higher switching frequencies of modern traction converters can lead to resonances in the Traction Power Supply System, which can lead to costly major malfunctions. At the same time compatibility must exist between the rolling stock and the train detection layer. This necessitates a careful fine tuning of the various system elements. As the railway system as a whole is a legacy system, in which for instance a large number of different systems are used for train detection, this is a complex and time consuming task, of which the importance is growing, illustrated for instance by the start of the EU STREP (Specific Targeted Research Project) Railcom. In Portugal the introduction of new rolling stock has lead to severe resonance problems in (traction) power supply systems. Before the introduction of a new switching frequency of the power invertors in the rolling stock it must be ascertained that not only no new problems with respect to resonances of the traction power supply system, but also with respect to the train detection layer (a safety critical system!) are introduced. A mutual project between REFER and Movares, with co-operation of CP (Comboios de Portugal), has been started to determine a solution, which is a technical and economical optimal solution. The project consists of 3 parts, homologation of the modified rolling stock with signalling and telecommunication installations, development and evaluation of a measurement system and modelling of traction power supply system. Two separate measurement campaigns are used to measure the compatibility with the train detection layer, a third measurement campaign for validation of the measurement system. The entire traction power supply network of Portugal (21 substations and 1430 km of line) has been modelled in the frequency range 100 Hz - 10 kHz. Using modelling it is possible to study the effect of the change in switching frequency and the different configurations of the traction power supply system more easily and more economical than using measurements. The simulation results compare well with the measurements performed. Using modern simulation tools and measurement techniques it is possible to reach compatibility between all elements of the railway system and prove that the RAMS (Reliability, Availability, Maintainability, Safety) requirements are met.

articleTitle: Propagation in Noisy Multipath Environment: Exactraction of Paths Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The characterization of double-directional channels has received considerable attention these last years since it is the starting point for the optimization of multiantenna wireless communication systems in a given environment. In fact, accurate double-directional model must reflect the spatial structure of the channel. Then, it is crucial to extract, from experimental data, the exact number and characteristics of the received paths. This task is particularly difficult when the signal to noise ratio (SNR) is rather low, scenario treated in this paper. Improvements are proposed to enhance the performances of paths number detection algorithms based on the eigenvalues of the correlation matrix. Two novel techniques are proposed in this paper. The first one is based on a new eigenvalues mean inequalities indicator whereas the second one integrates an eigenvalues oversampling method.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Interconnect Model for SI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents a new methodology for the transient analysis of lossy transmission lines. The proposed approach considers the Telegrapher's equations as a Sturm-Liouville problem. The Green's function is calculated in a series form and the open-end impedance matrix is obtained as the sum of infinite rational functions. This form permits an easy identification of poles and residues. Furthermore, the knowledge of poles leads to the development of a model order reduction technique by selecting only the dominant poles of the system within a fixed bandwidth. The pole-residue representation can then be synthesized in an equivalent circuit or converted into a state space model which can be easily interfaced with circuit Spice-like solvers. The numerical results confirm the accuracy of the proposed transmission line modelling technique.
