articleTitle: A Systematic Approach for Transient Analysis of Power Delivery Networks with Active Devices
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The analysis and the design of the Power Delivery Network (PDN) is crucial in the real world of high-speed and high-performance on-board systems. The aim of this paper is to describe a systematic approach to perform transient analyses of the PDN by employing a frequency domain characterization of the power-bus geometries obtained by means of the Cavity Model theory. The results are shown for a multilayer structure and the circuit simulated also includes a detailed model of an active device. The methodology described in this article sets the framework for a systematic approach for investigating both the PDN and the signal link paths in the time domain.

articleTitle: Physical Layer Signal Integrity Analysis of High-Speed Systems through the Combined Use of Digital and Analog Simulation Techniques EMC Workshop 14-17 June 2007, Paris France
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The continuous advancements in CMOS process technology are driving up the operating frequencies of digital Integrated Circuits (IC) to several gigabits per second. New generation of high speed digital buses have been developed to allow different ICs to exchange data at these multi-gigabit data rates such as PCI Express, FibreChannel, SATA, HDMI, etc. One of the main problems today in designing these types of systems is to make sure that the information that comes out of a high speed transmit IC is reliably taken to another high speed receiver IC via high speed channel components such as PCB (Printed Circuit Board) traces, backplanes, connectors, and cables. This class of problems falls within the definition of Signal Integrity. To avoid having to go through long and painful prototype troubleshooting sessions it is necessary to invest time up front in the design and characterization of the high speed channel. This paper reviews the different simulation technologies, and modeling techniques available in Agilent's Advanced Design System (ADS) that are required for an efficient design of a multi-gigabit high speed digital system.

articleTitle: Coupling of Transient Electromagnetic Fields to a Generic Missile Enclosure VIA Aperture and Wire Penetration
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Electronic components of a time critical system like an aircraft must be highly unsusceptible to electromagnetic influences. In order to predict the immunity of a missile against transient electromagnetic threats, not only the electromagnetic systems itself has to be investigated, but also the missile enclosure. Assuming a sufficient conductivity of the metallic enclosure, the shielding effectiveness will be reduced substantially by aperture and wire penetration. In this contribution, the shielding properties of a generic missile (GENEC) are investigated by means of a metallic hollow cylinder. Therefore, different measurements were carried out in time and frequency domain. Furthermore, numerical field calculations were performed with a method of moments (MoM) tool.

articleTitle: A Lossy Interconnect Modeling by S Parameters Measurements using a Synthesis Method of Lossy Nonuniform Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A modeling method of lossy interconnect by S parameters measurements is presented. In this method, interconnects are represented by the equivalent uniform or nonuniform transmission lines using the Inverse-FDTD method. This is a synthsis method to obtain lossy nonuniform transmission line per unit length parameters and has been obtained by reconstructing update equations of the one-dimensional FDTD method. Parameters distributions of the equivalent lossy nonuniform transmission line are decided by two kinds of criterias. One criteria is that the S parameters of equivalent transmission line become the same as the measured ones. Another criteria is that the refrected and transmitted waveforms of equivalent transmission line become the same as the waveforms obtained from measured ones. We show how the differences between them influence those model parameters. Moreover, how the measurement frequency range of the S parameter influences those model parameters of the equivalent circuit is shown.

articleTitle: Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI) Effects on Communications and Transportaton Systems: Problems and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper reviews the intentional electromagnetic threats that may be directed at communications and transportation systems. In addition, two different types of mitigation approaches are described. This is followed by a short description of the related standardization work being performed in the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC). The paper concludes with an introduction to the Special Session on IEMI.

articleTitle: Automatic Procedure for Shielding Effectiveness Measurement by Means of a Nested Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper presents an automatic procedure for the measurement of the shielding effectiveness (SE) by means of the nested reverberation chamber (RC). A software was developed to manage the great amount of data collected during the measurement. The nested was applied to determine the shielding properties of a commercial lossy material: ECCOSORB LS-30.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Total Power Radiated by Personal Electronic Devices in a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The paper deals about the use of a reverberation chamber for the measurement of the total radiated power from PEDs. The total power is also used to calculate the distant electric field, comparing results obtained with a unitary directivity and with the maximum expected one. Finally, the PEDs emission are compared with the aircraft system bands for the EMI analysis.

articleTitle: A Computational Tool for Inter-Vehicle Communications Channel Modelling
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The development of inter-vehicle communications networks needs the estimation of channel parameters in a time varying environment. A stochastic modelling of the environment suitable for IVC analysis has been introduced in the frame of an existent computational tool. It allows a realistic modelling of antennas and IVC scenario together with an and ultra wide band analysis combining full-wave methods with ray-tracing.

articleTitle: Laboratory Case Studies for PLC Applications Aboard Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: A preliminary study is presented to investigate on the possible use of the electrical power network for power line communication (PLC) onboard aircraft. The electrical power network with feeding in direct current (dc) at 28 V or in alternated current (ac) at 400 Hz is considered to be the transmission carrier for broadband communications. To verify the feasibility of a PLC system on-board aircraft, an experimental investigation is proposed analysing simple test cases realised in an EMC laboratory with the scope to simulate the aircraft environment.

articleTitle: Sensor Development for the ILDAS Project
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The In-flight Lightning Strike Damage Assessment System (ILDAS) project is to provide data concerning real lightning strike to aircraft and helicopters. A key element in the project is to define appropriate sensors for on-board lightning current sensors, mainly trough the magnetic field. This paper gives a general overview of the project and discusses the rationale and the selected sensors

articleTitle: Near Field Scanning of Transient Signal Propagation in Electronic Circuits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper shows a possibility to visualize signal propagation in electronic circuits. Instead of using various galvanic measurement points all over the circuit, a test method is shown which measures the radiated field of the printed circuit board. By use of a 2-dimensional positionable field probe it is possible to get an overview over the signals running on the different parts of the PCB. In order to measure transient disturbing signals and distinguish them from normal device operation, problems of probe design and triggering need to be discussed.

articleTitle: The Impact of the new EMC Directive 2004/108/EC for the Railway Industry EMC Europe 2007
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The new EMC Directive 2004/108/EC includes a number of changes as well as clarification and simplification when compared with the old EMC Directive, 89/336/EEC. This paper summarises the application of the new EMC Directive to the Railway Industry and identifies the changes and the new responsibilities placed on equipment manufacturers and infrastructure controllers. It raises concerns regarding: interpretation of the Directive: ‘state of the art’, ‘good engineering practices’, the fixed installation and the definition of responsible person and the role of the Notified Body.

articleTitle: Achievements and Future of Fid Technology for UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Generation of high voltage pulses with pulse duration from 100 ps to several nanoseconds and peak power from tens of megawatt to tens of gigawatt has always been a technical challenge. Until now it was possible to achieve such specifications only using spark gaps. However the disadvantages of that technology are widely known.

articleTitle: A near Field Injection Model Including Power Losses for Susceptibility Prediction in Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper introduces a complete simulation model of a near-field injection set-up, used to measure the immunity of integrated circuits to radiated near-field aggression. This model includes the measurement set-up itself, as well as the integrated circuit under test, its environment (printed circuit board, power supply) and finally power losses. Therefore, the amount of power injected through a near-field probe, triggering a malfunction of an integrated circuit (IC) according to a given criterion, can be identified and predicted at any frequency up to 1 GHz. The validation of this model is ensured through a comparison between measurement and simulation results.

articleTitle: Study of the Performance of Series Filtering to Avoid the Near-End and Far-End Coupling using Multimodal Models
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: High speed signal paths are often placed near other signal strips. This fact helps to increase the crosstalk between strips. Sometimes a series filter is used to avoid this coupling. In this paper, different filter configurations are tested and analyzed from a multimodal point of view (taking into account all the modes present). The results of these tests show where the unwanted signals should be filtered and how to avoid undesired effects.

articleTitle: The Application Intentional Electromagnetic Interference (IEMI) Detectors for Safety and Security
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: IEMI effects on embedded electronic systems carrying out time critical functions are extremely undesirable and could lead to breaches in security e.g. through loss of availability, or to safety incidents e.g. through loss of control. Communications systems, transportation systems and the infrastructures of either may be considered to have time critical features which could be adversely affected by EMI. The risk posed by IEMI to the safety and security of systems is extremely difficult to quantify and is poorly understood. It is considered that this is partly because of the evolving IEMI environment and partly because of uncertainties surrounding system upset and failure mechanisms. Given the uncertainties it is difficult to recommend the installation of specific cost effective hardening measures for risk mitigation, even though very effective countermeasures for EMI exist. Detection of IEMI is likely to be a useful step towards identification of the need for balanced and proportionate hardening and protection. This paper discusses the manifestation of IEMI disruption, explores the requirements for an IEMI detection system, and provides details of some deployed concepts.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Detection System of Cellular Phones Aboard Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The numerical prediction of the electromagnetic field distribution and the experimental detection of cellular phones onboard aircraft need an accurate numerical simulations and the implementation of a distributed network of sensors having a well defined sensitivity and frequency selectivity. The aim of this work is to present the feasibility of such network by means of numerical simulations and the results of the experimental characterization of a prototype of sensor to be used aboard aircraft.

articleTitle: Susceptibility Analysis of a Wireless Car Safety Related System
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: Measurements in combination with numerical simulations have been used in the analysis of a one-way digital radio communication system for a vehicle application. The system consists of a sensor and a receiver that both are placed in a car. Measured parameters include radiation gain pattern, TRP and TIS. The susceptibility to interfering sources has also been investigated. The measured results have been used for making computer models of the transmitting and receiving antennas. These models have then been used in numerical simulations in order to study the coupling/transmission between the sensor and receiver for different configurations. The result shows that measurements in combination with simulations are useful in order to implement new digital radio communication systems in a complex environment such as that in a vehicle.

articleTitle: RF Immunity of Digital Integrated Circuits: Measurements, Modeling and Validation
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: This paper demonstrates that the Mπlog technique, already proposed in the literature for the generation of accurate and efficient IC macromodels, can be extended to the prediction of device immunity effects. The proposed models account for both the functional and the out-of-band behaviour of devices. The IC models are generated from port device responses only and can be implemented in any commercial tool based on SPICE or VHDL-AMS solvers. The approach is demonstrated on a real test board by injecting a RF noise disturbance into a digital IC: a systematic study comparing actual measurements and simulation predictions is carried out.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Study of the Electromagnetic Environment Generated inside a Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2007 International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility - EMC Europe
abstract: The actual standards propose the Reverberation Chamber as an alternative test facility for radiated immunity tests on automotive equipment. The question usually asked is how the Reverberation Chamber's environment can be compared to an automotive vehicle's one. In order to give some answers to this question, this article will analyze and discuss the results concerning the field probability density function in both environments. Data will be collected by simulation. Both references are LASMEA's Reverberation Chamber and a vehicle.
